quote: I often say, when I make these little observations, ‘Had Aristotle cooked, he would have written a great deal more.’
source: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, The Answer, on the philosophies of the kitchen, p. 75 (trans. Electa Arenal and Amanda Powell, 1994)
note: The printed page was not seen. The wording follows Arenal and Powell as two scholars quote it, Julie Bokser in Rhetoric Review and Theresa Yugar, both citing page 75. Edith Grossman's 2014 translation ends the same way, so a splice of the two cannot be ruled out until page 75 is opened.

evidence.where: Two scholars quoting Arenal and Powell page 75, not the page itself. Julie Bokser, Sor Juana's Rhetoric of Silence, Rhetoric Review 25:1 (2006), whose works cited names the 1994 Feminist Press edition and whose block quote closes (75). Theresa A. Yugar, a Sor Juana monographer, at Feminism and Religion, 17 April 2017, cites (Arenal & Powell, The Response, 75) and gives the identical sentence; she also quotes the preceding sentence, what then shall I tell you, my Lady, of the secrets of nature that I have learned while cooking, which Bokser's block does not contain, so she was reading the page and not copying Bokser. The rival translation was read verbatim: the epigraph of Chicana/Latina Studies 20:1 (Fall 2020), credited Grossman, 2014, 184 to 185, reads And seeing these minor details, I say that if Aristotle had cooked, he would have written a great deal more, so Grossman shares only the tail and not the framing clause. Pamela Kirk Rappaport, Paulist Press 2005, printed at Lapham's Quarterly, reads written much more, a different tail. evidence.edition: The Answer / La Respuesta, ed. and trans. Electa Arenal and Amanda Powell (The Feminist Press at CUNY, 1994), p. 75
evidence.locator: In the passage on the secrets of nature learned while cooking, a few lines after what can we women know, save philosophies of the kitchen

reason: The sentence is securely Sor Juana's, nothing is minted, and the framing clause is a faithful rendering of Y yo suelo decir viendo estas cosillas, so the doubt is about translation wording only and never about authorship. I added the witness the refuter lacked: Yugar cites Arenal and Powell at page 75 with the identical wording and quotes a sentence Bokser's block does not contain, which argues independent access, and Grossman's head is wholly different, so two scholars splicing at the same mid sentence point is improbable. But nobody in this chain has opened page 75, so the doubt survives rather than dies, and the honest ruling is a hedge whose note names the gap instead of a verification that claims a page nobody read. shipped.js returns no match and no near match, Sor Juana is at 0 of 3 and not banned, she is not in the misattribution list, Correspondence is right for the Respuesta, and the source is 127 characters with no dash. The editor should weigh two things: the theme fit is the thinnest part, since this is knowledge in ordinary work rather than renewal or the road, and the quotation's last character is the closing mark of the nested quotation, which sits just after the full stop rule 32 asks for.
